_doc: T-3804. The 1871 street walls round the jaunt stops: per-street profiles read from the period street views, a restyle of each generated shop front on the stops' block faces, new attached fronts where a face had only side walls and gaps, and the named buildings the stops look at. Written by tools/build_1871_street_walls.py; read by renderers/web/js/city-context.js, built by renderers/web/js/city-fronts.js. Every form is reconstructed (L-1871-street-walls) unless a building says otherwise.

lake.label: Lake Street, the old wholesale row
lake.note: Carbutt's 'Lake street, East from Clark': attached four- and five-storey fronts party wall to party wall, segmental and round-headed windows in hooded surrounds, bracketed cornices, lettered friezes, cast-iron shop fronts under awnings. The late-1860s Lake Street stereoview in the owner's references (rights not yet traced, so read only) shows the same row with cream stone fronts, a mansard or two, round-arched iron arcades and an iron balcony.

clark_square.label: Clark Street facing the Court House square
clark_square.note: Carbutt's 'Clark street, North from Washington': on the east side, facing the square, one long pale stone front of five storeys, its windows round-headed in even rows, an iron balcony along the first upper storey, a lettered frieze under the cornice and an arched ground floor under awnings.

clark.label: Clark Street
clark.note: Carbutt's Clark Street view: pale stone and brick fronts of four and five storeys, round and segmental heads, awnings.

state.label: State Street
state.note: Carbutt's 'Book Seller's Row, State Street': a five-storey pale stone ('Athens marble') front of identical units, round-arched windows in even rows, a heavy bracketed cornice, iron and glass shop fronts under awnings.

lasalle.label: LaSalle Street
lasalle.note: Carbutt's Chamber of Commerce card shows across LaSalle a brick block of five storeys under a tall mansard; Kurz's 1865 'La Salle Street from Court House Square' in the owner's references (rights not yet traced, so read only) shows the street as attached stone fronts of four and five storeys with arched windows, several under mansards.

cross.label: Randolph, Washington, Madison and Dearborn
cross.note: The business streets between: Carbutt's Lake Street and Crosby's Opera House cards show four- and five-storey brick and stone fronts, segmental heads on the brick, round on the stone, bracketed cornices.

buildings.name: St. James Hotel
buildings.identity: Edwards' 1871 directory: 'St. James Hotel, Washington Libbey propr. State, nw. cor. Washington'. Andreas (vol. 2, p. 508): the Stewart House at the corner of State and Washington, 'including Nos. 92, 94, 96 and 98' State, reopened as the Merchants' Hotel, burnt, 're-built on a larger scale' and opened in January 1868 as the St. James, kept by Libby & Harlow until the fire.
buildings.place: The State Street front from the Washington corner north over the three generated rows there (about 41 m, the corner and Nos. 92-98 at the directory's spacing), and its Washington Street front from the corner west to Crosby's.
buildings.form: Carbutt's card of Crosby's Opera House shows the corner building beside it before 1868: five storeys of brick, paired round-arched windows in hooded surrounds on three upper storeys, an arcaded attic of small arched windows under a bracketed cornice with blocks along its parapet, a shop storey under awnings. The St. James that replaced it in 1867-68 is not pictured; it is built in the same form at the same height, which is reconstructed.

buildings.name: Brick block west of Crosby's Opera House
buildings.identity: Unnamed: the front standing against Crosby's west wall in Carbutt's card. Its owner and firms are not identified.
buildings.place: The first generated row west of the opera house on Washington Street, as the card shows it.
buildings.form: The card shows five storeys of red brick, plain segmental-headed sash windows on stone sills, round-headed windows in the top storey, a heavy cornice on large scroll brackets, and a ground storey of windows and an arched door over an areaway rather than a shop front.

buildings.name: McVicker's Theatre
buildings.identity: Edwards' 1871 directory lists McVicker's Theatre on 'Madison, bet. Dearborn and State'; Andreas (vol. 2, pp. 597-599) gives its building in 1857 and its remodelling in 1871, when 'nothing but the walls of the old theater remained', reopened on 29 August, six weeks before the fire.
buildings.place: On Madison Street's south side east of the Tribune building, over the two generated rows there; its exact lots are not recorded, so the place along the block is reconstructed.
buildings.form: Andreas's engraving (p. 598) of the 1857 theatre: a four-storey brick front with corniced hoods over its windows, a bracketed cornice with the name lettered under it, a belvedere over the middle with its own cornice and flagstaff, and an iron colonnade carrying a balcony across the ground storey. The 1871 remodelling kept the walls, so the front is taken as the engraving shows it; that it kept its porch and belvedere is reconstructed.

buildings.name: Marble front facing the Court House square
buildings.identity: Unnamed: the long pale stone front Carbutt photographed on the east side of Clark Street from Washington north. The directory places the firms in it by number; the building itself is not named in the sources read.
buildings.place: Clark Street's east side between Washington and Randolph, opposite the Court House square.
buildings.form: Five storeys of pale stone under one heavy cornice, round-headed windows in even rows, an iron balcony along the first upper storey, an arched ground floor under awnings.
